definitions.gloss: commemorative photo; souvenir photo; memorial photograph
definitions.explanation: A photograph taken to commemorate a special occasion, event, or visit to a notable place.

examples.japanese: {記念写真|きねんしゃしん}を{撮|と}ろう。
{卒業式|そつぎょうしき}で{記念写真|きねんしゃしん}を{撮|と}った。
examples.english: We took a commemorative photo at the graduation ceremony.

examples.japanese: {観光地|かんこうち}で{家族|かぞく}みんなで{記念写真|きねんしゃしん}を{撮|と}ってもらった。
examples.english: We had someone take a group commemorative photo of our whole family at the tourist spot.

notes:
A compound of {記念|きねん} (commemoration, memorial) and {写真|しゃしん} (photograph). A ubiquitous concept in Japanese culture, where taking {記念写真|きねんしゃしん} is a standard part of ceremonies, school events, travel, and social gatherings.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {記念写真|きねんしゃしん}を{撮|と}る: to take a commemorative photo
- {記念写真|きねんしゃしん}を{撮|と}ってもらう: to have someone take a commemorative photo
- {集合|しゅうごう}{記念写真|きねんしゃしん}: group commemorative photo
- {記念写真|きねんしゃしん}{撮影|さつえい}: commemorative photo shoot

USAGE:
At Japanese events like {入学式|にゅうがくしき} (entrance ceremonies), {卒業式|そつぎょうしき} (graduations), {結婚式|けっこんしき} (weddings), and company events, taking a {記念写真|きねんしゃしん} is almost obligatory. At tourist sites, it is common to ask strangers or staff to take your photo — the phrase {記念写真|きねんしゃしん}を{撮|と}っていただけますか is frequently used.
